simulator.title: Simulate new transactions
simulator.hint: Creates a synthetic ingestion after the current dataset's last day and queues processing.
simulator.countHint: From 50 to 5,000 synthetic transactions resampled from the dataset's recent history.
simulator.countError: Enter a whole number between 50 and 5,000 transactions.
simulator.daysHint: Span of 1 to 7 days starting the day after the latest recorded transaction.
simulator.daysError: Enter a whole number between 1 and 7 days.
simulator.fanOutHint: Adds one account receiving funds and dispersing them to multiple new counterparties during the simulated period.

settings.title: Processing
settings.description: Settings applied to the active dataset. Manual processing remains available on Data sources.
settings.autoHint: When enabled, the worker automatically schedules continuous processing for this dataset at the interval below, recalculating the open period whenever new transactions arrive. When off, processing only runs manually from Data sources.
settings.intervalHint: Wait time between automatic runs, from 5 to 1,440 minutes (24 hours). Saving while automation is enabled recalculates the next run from now.
settings.intervalError: Enter a whole number between 5 and 1,440 minutes.
settings.sampleHint: Randomly draws 0 to 50 active accounts outside the model's queue each week (0 disables it), regardless of risk score, for analyst review. Used to estimate laundering the model missed and reduce bias when retraining with analyst feedback.
settings.sampleScope: These accounts appear at the end of the queue with the "Control sample" badge, are excluded from alert rates and suspicious accounts, and changes apply to weeks processed from now on.
settings.sampleError: Enter a whole number between 0 and 50 accounts per week.
settings.simulatorToggle: Show transaction simulator on Data sources
settings.simulatorHint: Displays the "Simulate transactions" button on Data sources to generate synthetic transactions (50 to 5,000 rows across 1 to 7 days, with an optional fan-out pattern) and queue processing. Simulations still in the open period can be removed as long as no analyst decision exists.
